handbookNote: The official Massachusetts boating handbook developed for the Massachusetts Environmental Police (MEP), delivered through MEP-approved course providers (Boat-Ed/Kalkomey and iLearnToBoat) -- Massachusetts has no single official state-administered boating knowledge exam; a boater satisfies the state mandate by passing the exam embedded in an MEP-approved course, which both Boat-Ed and iLearnToBoat independently confirm requires an 80% minimum passing score on unit quizzes and the final exam, with unlimited retake attempts (this 80%/unlimited-attempts convergence matches this project's WA/AZ boating precedent) -- the exact final-exam question count is not consistently published by either MEP-approved vendor and is therefore left unconfirmed rather than asserted (a third, non-MEP-approved vendor, BoatUS Foundation, separately advertises 60 final-exam questions, but its course is explicitly stated NOT to satisfy Massachusetts's mandatory education requirement, so that figure is not treated as confirming MEP-approved-course convergence) -- Massachusetts's mandate itself is a genuine, currently phasing-in law confirmed independently by both MEP-approved vendors: operators of motorboats and PWCs must complete an approved course and carry proof aboard, with boaters born after January 1, 1989 required to certify by April 1, 2026 (no penalties until September 1, 2026) and boaters born on or before January 1, 1989 given until April 1, 2028; minimum operating ages are 12 for a motorboat and 16 for a PWC; this newer universal mandate layers on top of a narrower pre-existing MA requirement (noted by BoatUS Foundation) that already required an approved course for boaters under 16 and PWC operators under 18 -- content also grounded in Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 90B (Motorboats, Mooring of Vessels, Regattas, Marine Parks, Piers, and Boat Launching Areas), which establishes vessel registration, reckless/negligent operation, and marine operating-under-the-influence (OUI) provisions enforced by the Massachusetts Environmental Police, plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (PFDs, required equipment, Navigation Rules, aids to navigation, cold-water immersion relevant to Massachusetts's New England climate, and nor'easter/fog weather hazards specific to the Massachusetts coast); federal boating-accident-reporting deadlines (48 hours / 10 days) are presented as the general baseline since a Massachusetts-specific deviation from that federal threshold was not independently re-verified against the exact state statute in this build -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
